run.incident_title: Soul Song Service: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'requestMetadata')

feedback_for_repair: Keep the createRequest fix; it directly addresses the undefined requestMetadata crash.
Revert the no-op captureHandledError stubs unless you can prove the monitoring import is broken.
Restore a single valid Stimpact integration in main.tsx instead of removing installation entirely.
Minimize the patch to the incident-related code path and add targeted verification of the request creation UI flow.
requested_checks: Run the frontend flow that triggers createRequest and confirm the TypeError is gone.
Verify whether ../stimpact or @stimpact/sdk/vite should be the canonical integration, and keep a single working installation rather than removing monitoring entirely.
Exercise code paths in queryClient.ts and xanoClient.ts that call captureHandledError to confirm reporting still occurs and no type/runtime issues remain.
Check whether main.tsx originally had a duplicate import/install bug; if so, fix it minimally with one valid import and one install call.

risks.reasoning: Imports of captureHandledError were replaced with local no-op functions in queryClient.ts and xanoClient.ts, and Stimpact installation was removed from main.tsx. This appears to fully disable handled error reporting and app initialization for the monitoring service, which is a significant behavioral regression unrelated to the null dereference itself.

The createRequest change is well aligned with the reported error message, but the patch also removes duplicate/possibly conflicting Stimpact setup without evidence that this contributed to the incident. The extra edits increase blast radius and reduce confidence.

Verification only ran a production build. There is no evidence of exercising the frontend request creation flow or confirming that handled errors and app startup behavior still work after removing monitoring hooks.
